summary: Implemented owner-scoped automations with authenticated manual, schedule, webhook and allowlisted-command triggers; immutable versioned agent/skill profiles; idempotent leased run materialization; snapshot-bound tasks; cancel/replay; append-only audit; and a real API-backed accessible Portal control center.

scopeExpansion.reason: Owner identity, durable scheduling, crash recovery, immutable run manifests, and runtime-only scheduler/webhook credentials require shared server-principal, D1 schema, Compose and documentation changes beyond the declared app/lib/db surface.

acceptanceEvidence.ownershipAndScope: Browser bodies cannot choose an actor. Hosted identity is trusted only with an explicit server flag; local operation requires a short-lived signed human identity scoped to the workspace. Every profile, automation, run, event and snapshot query is owner/workspace scoped.
acceptanceEvidence.versionedProfiles: Agent and skill definitions are schema-bounded and stored as append-only versions. Database triggers reject profile UPDATE and DELETE. Automations pin exact agent and skill versions, and every run stores those exact definitions in an immutable snapshot manifest.
acceptanceEvidence.safeTriggers: Manual and named-command runs require the signed owner. Schedules require an exact-body HMAC scheduler principal and compare-and-swap due-slot claim. Webhooks require exact-body HMAC authentication. Paused automations cannot create new runs.
acceptanceEvidence.idempotencyAndRecovery: Run reservation uses a unique automation/idempotency key before task creation. Materialization uses a bounded lease, deterministic task/snapshot/event inserts, expired-lease recovery, and lease-owner finalization.
acceptanceEvidence.approvalBoundary: Automations create planning tasks and proposals only. Generated task goals explicitly require human approval before file mutation, command execution, commit, push, merge or publication; no route can auto-approve or auto-execute a proposal.
acceptanceEvidence.cancelAndReplay: Cancellation withdraws pending approvals, cancels the task, clears leases and records an append-only event. Replay derives the original owner-scoped automation but creates a fresh run, task and repository snapshot.
acceptanceEvidence.portal: The Automations tab edits typed agent/skill profiles, selects exact immutable versions, builds all four trigger types, pauses/resumes, runs allowed triggers, and exposes snapshot-bound history, immutable events, cancellation and replay. Local identity tokens remain page-memory input and are not persisted.

reviewerBlockerCorrections.pausedReplay: Both direct run and replay now fail with automation_paused when the owner has paused the automation.
reviewerBlockerCorrections.snapshotUniqueness: Each run receives a cryptographically random UUID snapshot identifier; the immutable manifest still captures the exact base/head and profile versions.
reviewerBlockerCorrections.schedulerRecovery: A scheduled slot is reserved/materialized before next_run_at advances, exact-slot eligibility is checked during reservation, and every expired schedule:* materializer lease is recovered independently of the current next_run_at.
reviewerBlockerCorrections.webhookScopeBinding: The webhook HMAC now covers workspace ID, hook ID and exact request body bytes, preventing reuse of a valid signature against another route scope.
reviewerBlockerCorrections.cancelRace: Run cancellation is a conditional state transition; approval/task changes and the audit insert are conditioned on that exact committed timestamp. A concurrent completion yields 409 without mutating the completed task or its pending approval.

checks.summary: 10 focused tests passed for bounded triggers/profiles, owner authentication, scheduler/webhook scope binding, approval gating, idempotent reservation, crash recovery, cancellation race safety and immutable profile/event/snapshot data.
Drizzle read all 20 tables and reported no schema changes; migration metadata is coherent.
TypeScript validation passed after the final automation hardening changes.
ESLint passed after the final automation hardening changes.
Production build passed after reviewer corrections; 117 application tests passed, 0 failed, 1 opt-in live harness skipped; 18 companion tests passed, 0 failed.
Full Playwright runtime suite passed 8/8, including authenticated Automations profile creation, trigger creation, queued run, audit detail and cancellation.

checks.command: temporary scheduler secret + docker compose web rebuild + npm run test:automation-live + secret removal/recreate
checks.summary: Live Docker API created immutable profiles and automations, proved duplicate run idempotency, cancellation, fresh replay, paused run/replay rejection, unsigned scheduler rejection, signed scheduler acceptance, workspace+hook-bound webhook acceptance, and cross-hook signature replay rejection. The web container was then recreated without either temporary secret; final runtime ready=true, scheduler=false and webhook=false.

externalActions: No commit, push, merge, publication, provider mutation, secret persistence or secret rotation was performed.
